versions.changes: New app icon (green mountains with a gold line to the summit) on the program, shortcuts, taskbar and window, and on the profile and PIN screens. Retirement: the margin loan's interest before retirement is added to the loan or paid from your pay (your choice); repaying the loan at retirement shows as a sale with its capital gain in the first year; a fall below the maintenance margin triggers a margin call (holdings sold to repay part of the loan) in the simple results and in Monte Carlo, which also shows how often margin calls happened; a warning when the loan costs more than the holdings earn. Retirement page: narrower input boxes, spending goals are the Fixed Goal policy, and the withdrawal strategy is chosen in the comparison card. Buttons look the same throughout the app. Privacy: the published source zip holds only the program (no tests, sample files or tools), every release is checked for personal data before it is published, and updates delete data files that older source updates left behind.

Hang recorder: if Summit freezes or is slow to start, the log notes each startup step and where the program is stuck (page names and program lines only: no figures, names, accounts, searches or addresses; your Windows user folder shows as %USERPROFILE%). Import: the CRA's My Account "List of all slips" PDF is split into one slip each (T4, T5, T5008, T3, RRSP receipt, TFSA records, T4FHSA and more) and checked against slips you already saved: identical ones aren't saved twice, different figures are listed. Questrade monthly statement PDFs (also zipped), the Activities download (Excel) and trade confirmations (CSV) are read without duplicating each other, whatever order you import them; month-end holdings on statements are checked against Summit's units. Tables keep the column you sorted by after saving, filtering or reopening.

Taxes > Investments, per the CRA's timing rules: only distributions from funds, ETFs, trusts and REITs move to the year of their record date; dividends from companies count in the year they are paid. Sales count in the year they settle (a December 31 trade settling in January is next year's), using Wealthsimple's settlement date. Margin interest: choose whether each charge counts on the date it was charged (the default) or for the month it covers (charged on the 1st for last month); the CRA accepts either if you use the same one every year.

Overview works without investments: net worth, Assets and Liabilities, and a net worth chart built from bank and card balances. Profiles: the lock screen has Switch profile; Forgot PIN asks for the date of birth saved in the profile (the name is not accepted, wrong answers count like wrong PINs); date of birth is now required in User Info (the owner's for a corporation). Tax documents: User Info has an optional Last 3 digits of your SIN; a slip whose SIN ends differently is flagged as possibly someone else's and set to Don't save. T5013, T4RSP, T4RIF, T4A, NR4, T4 and T4E are recognised with every box saved; T5013 amounts count on Taxes > Investments (capital gains, interest, dividends, foreign income and tax, carrying charges, return of capital) and a T4RSP's Home Buyers' Plan withdrawal (box 27) is checked against your HBP. Taxes > Investments: distributions paid in January but on record in December (for example VEQT's year-end distribution) count in the record date's year, with the return of capital and non-cash distribution posted with them; interest from personal bank accounts counts as investment income; T3 foreign income (box 25) is added to both sides of the interest check. Settings shows only the message from what you just did, not the page's own warnings.

Business and rental transactions on Spending: the Category column is now the tax form line, with only that form's lines (income lines for money in, expense lines for money out) and Transfer, Owner draw, Capital purchase, Loan principal, GST/HST and the new Ignore (not on the tax form); guesses show in italics until you confirm them (or tick rows and use Tax use > Confirm the guessed tax lines). Add your own labels (for example Snow removal) under a form line from the same menu; they also appear on Taxes > Business and Rental. Spending shows months that only have business or rental transactions. PIN: every profile now needs a 4-digit PIN (Settings opens on Security until one is created; it can be changed, not removed). Settings > Data has two delete options, Delete all transactions and Delete this profile, each confirmed in a window with your PIN (no more typing DELETE; Delete all data is gone); Forgot PIN deletes only that profile's data after a confirmation. Import: a file with only column headings (a year with no activity) shows as an empty file and is skipped, not an error; files from a folder show their subfolder and are listed in order; Wealthsimple chequing and credit card exports are named Wealthsimple. Which way amounts go is decided by the rows' own types when a file has them (withdrawals negative and deposits positive, or the reverse), and the preview's sample always shows money in and money out. A statement with a Balance column sets the account's opening balance so Summit's balance matches the bank's (only while the opening balance is 0). Overview: with one line on the chart, the y-axis fits that line instead of starting at $0. Pages no longer have a title and description at the top; the Import button on the Transactions pages is gone (use the upload icon or drop files anywhere). The Profiles page is shorter. Date of birth accepts only a real date with a 4-digit year from 1900 to today, and every date field is limited to 4-digit years. Running the program from Downloads no longer creates a data folder there unless you choose to run it from there.

Uninstall (Settings > Apps > Summit > Uninstall) is one question: it closes Summit if it is open and removes everything it created on this computer: the program, every profile and its data, settings, update backups, the Start menu and desktop shortcuts and the Apps entry. Protected backups you saved elsewhere (and your automatic backup folder) are not touched. Everything Summit keeps is now in its own program folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Investment Tracker): it no longer creates %APPDATA%\InvestTracker (data on a read-only install, the install question's answer) or %LOCALAPPDATA%\InvestTracker (update build files); folders made by older versions are moved in or removed at start-up. Pages still open if the data file can't be read.

Tax documents: nothing is kept from an uploaded document except its figures: the PDF is held in memory only until you save (never written to disk) and its text is no longer stored, so no personal details are kept; documents imported before are read again with the improved reader and their stored text deleted. Notices of Assessment: every figure is now read (the CRA prints amounts without a $ sign): the summary lines (15000, 23600, 26000, 42000, 43500, 43700 and others), refund or balance owing, next year's RRSP deduction limit and available room, pension adjustment, next year's FHSA room and the Canada training credit limit; Contribution Room uses the FHSA room from the notice. TFSA transactions statements (Wealthsimple and others) are recognised: each contribution and withdrawal is read and used for your TFSA room (marked 'statement', yellow when your transactions differ). Wealthsimple T5008 slips laid out as a table of trades are read (each trade, totals in boxes 16, 20 and 21); Canadian ShareOwner shown as the issuer of its T3 slips. Taxes > Investments: click an imported slip to see everything read from it (every box with its description, the Notice of Assessment lines, RRSP receipt periods, TFSA statement entries, T5008 trades). Import: drop files or folders anywhere in Summit and the preview opens straight away (a 'Drop to import' box shows while dragging); the Import window has one drop area for files and folders together, a Choose files button, and a list you can add to and remove from before importing; Import files is gone from the menu (use the upload icon in the top bar). Business and rental: better starting tax labels: an e-transfer from someone else is rent or sales (not a transfer between your accounts), damage deposits and deposit refunds, laundry income, owner draws and contributions, card payments, GST/HST remittances, and common payees (office supplies, courier, software, coworking rent, travel, meals, insurance, utilities, property tax, repairs, snow removal and lawn care, advertising); returns are no longer counted as sales and a replacement or renovation is guessed as a capital purchase. Sample statements for trying business and rental features are in sample_data/rental_business_test.

Profiles: keep separate sets of data on one computer (two people, or your personal books and a corporation's). Each profile has its own accounts, transactions, settings, PIN and encrypted data file; if there is more than one, Summit asks which to open at start-up, and the top-right menu has Switch profile. A profile is named by its User Info (your name, or the company name for a corporation) and renamed when you change it. Settings > Data > Delete this profile permanently deletes the open profile (Delete account is gone). Corporation profiles (a one-owner Canadian-controlled private corporation such as a professional corporation or a contracting company, any province or territory): Taxes gets T2 Summary (net income for tax with Schedule 1, taxable income, small business deduction with the passive-income grind, federal and provincial tax at 2025 and 2026 rates prorated for mid-year changes, Part IV tax, refundable tax and the dividend refund, NERDTOH, ERDTOH, capital dividend account, GRIP, losses carried forward, instalments and balance owing), Income Statement (GIFI 125, from the corporation's labelled bank and card transactions), Balance Sheet (GIFI 100) and GST/HST (by annual, quarterly or monthly period); a new Company tab has Owner Pay (salary with T4 boxes, eligible, other and capital dividends with T5 boxes, shareholder loan with a one-year repayment warning) and Corporate Info (province, BN, GST/HST rate, opening balances). Personal-only pages are hidden in a corporation profile. Update backups are made only for profiles whose data changed since their last backup, plus before Clear data. Settings > Modules: Overview chart default view (timeframe, dollars or % change, everything or net worth only; or the last used).

Business and rental, linked to your accounts: an account can be marked Used for a business or rental property on the Accounts page (everything from it goes to that tax page); on mixed accounts, tag transactions with Tax use on Spending (one at a time or several at once), or make a rule (descriptions containing… -> business or property, label, share), applied to every import. One record: nothing is copied; entries copied from Spending before are turned into links once. Plain-words tax labels per kind (Rent, Damage or security deposit held, Property taxes, Sales or fees, Meals 50%, Owner draw, Capital purchase, Loan principal, Transfer…) with the T776/T2125 line shown; labels guessed from the spending category until you confirm; Personal takes a transaction off the forms; a business or rental share % for mixed-use costs. GST/HST: choose the rate a registered business charges; sales and taxable purchases are split into the amount and the GST/HST; a separate label for remittances and refunds. Tax pages list the linked bank and card transactions with editable labels, and Rental shows deposits held. Spending: business and rental transactions are left out of spending totals by default (Settings > Modules to include them); coloured tags and a Tax use filter. Overview: business and rental this year so far. All of this appears only for businesses or properties you have, and not for a module you turned off unless it has data.

Taxes: one Tax year selector for every Taxes page, at the right of the sub-tabs (remembered between visits); page titles removed on the Taxes pages; an Import button (upload icon) in the top bar on every page. Contribution Room: RRSP contributions now come from the deposits into your RRSP accounts (like TFSA), checked against imported receipts (yellow when they disagree, editable); new Home Buyers' Plan section: tick RRSP withdrawals as HBP (or add one by hand), repayment schedule over 15 years (starting the second year after, or the fifth year for a first withdrawal from 2022 to 2028), minimum = balance / years left, designated repayments editable and taken off deductible contributions, shortfall shown as income on line 12900; Tax Summary shows lines 24600 and 12900. Import: the More options section is gone. Each bank or card file is worked out on its own (which amounts are money out, the kind of account, the bank's name) and the preview shows the guess with sample rows; you can change the account (existing or new), kind and sign per file before saving, and a file that could be read either way is marked Please check. A Wealthsimple statement asks which account it is from on the preview. Fixed the drop hint showing twice in the Import dialog.

Encryption at rest (Windows): your data is stored only encrypted (AES-256-GCM, using Windows' own cryptography), with a key that Windows keeps for your Windows sign-in, so a copy of the file can't be read on another computer or by another Windows account; nothing to type or remember. On first start the existing database is encrypted, checked, and the plain file overwritten and removed; older update backups are encrypted the same way. While Summit runs the data is decrypted only in memory and written back encrypted after every change. Settings > Data: shows whether your data is encrypted, Export protected backup (a file encrypted with a passphrase you choose, which opens on any computer) and Restore protected backup. If this Windows account can't unlock the data (new PC, reset profile) a page offers to restore a protected backup; the locked file is never changed. Settings > Security: optional Automatic backup to another location (USB drive, network or OneDrive folder), daily or weekly, keeping the newest 3, 5 or 10; the passphrase is never stored. Update backups: the 3 newest are kept (was 10). Tax documents: every box and the text of each slip are saved (boxes the app doesn't use yet too), with your SIN, name and address removed first; the PDF itself is not kept; unrecognised documents are kept as Other tax document. Older versions can't read the encrypted file: rolling back below this version shows an empty app until you update again (nothing is lost).

Renamed to Summit, with a new icon (charcoal and gold mountains with a rising line) and a Charcoal and gold colour choice in Settings > Display; the program file and install folder keep their old names, and the Start menu shortcut no longer shows a SmartScreen warning after an update. Navigation: Overview, Accounts, Transactions (Investments and Spending), Taxes (Summary, Investments, Business, Rental, Contribution Room) and Calculators (Retirement, Mortgage, Margin); Market & Reference Data and Import files are in the top-right menu. One owner: Ownership, Spouse and Joint are gone; everything is yours with one cost base per security (accounts that were Joint or Spouse are listed once in Settings > Data); rental co-owner and business partner shares stay. Import anywhere: drop CSV exports or PDF tax documents on any page; T3, T5, T5008, T4FHSA, RRSP contribution receipts and Notices of Assessment are recognised and read (type can be changed on the preview, amounts corrected before saving; the same file is never saved twice). Investment Taxes (was Cost base & gains): Schedule 3 with each line number under its amount, line 4 detail with options listed separately in contracts and each sale opening to its cost base history, T3 box 21 to line 17400 and T5 box 18 to 17600, line 25300 from your Notice of Assessment, investment income for Schedule 4 (12000, 12010, 12100, 13000, foreign tax 40500, return of capital), carrying charges (22100) with margin interest by month, T1135 foreign property, and the cost base of what you still hold. Every amount is filled in (slips first, then transactions) and can be typed over: edited amounts are italic with a reset, and a cell turns yellow when the sources disagree (listed under Check these). Business Taxes and Rental Taxes lines can be typed over the same way. Written options: the premium is now a capital gain in the year the option is written; buying it back in a later year is a loss in that year. Exchange rates: missing USD rates are filled from the Bank of Canada (the day's rate, or the business day before, for trades; the annual average for dividends and interest once the year is over); rates you entered are never changed. New Contribution Room page (TFSA moved from Accounts; RRSP from your Notice of Assessment and receipts; FHSA from T4FHSA slips) and Tax Summary page (each page's result with its T1 line).

New modules: Rental property (CRA form T776) and Business (CRA form T2125), each with its own tab that can be hidden in Settings > Modules. Per property or business and tax year: income and expenses under the form's line numbers with what belongs on each line, personal-use portion, co-owner or partner share, motor vehicle costs at business km / total km (business parking in full, passenger-vehicle limits), capital assets with CCA by class (half-year rule, accelerated investment incentive, recapture, terminal loss, vehicles over the ceiling in class 10.1), rental CCA kept from creating a loss for all properties combined, short-term rental non-compliance, cost of goods sold with inventory, meals at 50%, business-use-of-home limited to business income with carry-forward, GST/HST collected and input tax credits, a review list like Cost base (missing kilometres or home %, large repairs that may be capital, undescribed other expenses), Add from Spending (copies chosen transactions; Spending is not changed) and a CSV of the form lines. No other page was changed.

Tables: columns are aligned as a whole — number columns ($, %, amounts, number boxes) are right-aligned with their header, including “–” and “by hand”; text columns stay left. Sorting: click a column title to sort the Accounts tables (investment, chequing/savings, assets, liabilities) and the Transactions list; Spending transactions sort across all entries, not just the ones shown. Filters now sit inside the transaction table card, above the column they filter (month, search, account, type/category); the table title is inside the card. Overview: card titles removed; the net worth chart has its own row; holdings, assets and liabilities sit side by side in one card with their titles inside (on a phone each becomes its own card). Spending: the chart is full width; the pie chart sits beside one card holding By category and Average per month by group. Retirement: the My Account Values button (was Use my current balances & account settings) sits under Balance today and fills only that column — it no longer resets Return % to 5% or changes yearly additions; Added per year comes before Return %/yr; Dividend and Interest yield are columns on the Non-registered row.

Accounts: Account ID is a column in each account row; the Done button is gone (changes save when you click out of a field, click the row again to close it); “Real cash today” and “Opening cash adjustment” are removed from investment accounts (existing adjustments are kept); Closed and Ignore in net worth are larger; the transaction count is at the far right of the edit bar. Layout: a leftover 1% column-width rule made tables stretch to full width and squeezed their last columns; tables are now as wide as their contents, centered, with roomier cells, and page side margins are about double the 2.6.1 width on wide screens. Market and Tax Data: the Start-up checks card is removed. Spending: new Search descriptions box in the filters (description, note and category). Fix: entries left on a deleted category (or any category no longer in the list) now become Uncategorized, so they can be filtered and appear in the Uncategorized card; learned merchants and built-in keywords for deleted categories are no longer used. Categories: new default list by group (Home, Food, Auto, Spending, Bills & Subscriptions, Travel, Health & Fitness, Financial, Income & Transfers, Other) with one name per category; a bank’s own wording for a category (Internet and phone, Dining, Gas, parking, and tolls…) is filed under the matching existing category instead of creating a second one, and categories already kept under two names are merged once (their entries move with them).

Import: files can be loaded one by one, several at once, or a whole folder (only CSV/TXT files in it are read). Raw rows: every imported row is stored exactly as in the file (description, date, time, whole raw row); renaming or changing account type only changes how it is shown, and duplicates are found by comparing raw rows. Deleted assets and liabilities, and deleted accounts, are removed from history; past net worth is built from the Historic values table, which now also lists ignored accounts, and closed accounts show $0. Charts: month-to-date income is cumulative, income is hidden on 30 and 90 days, and 30/90 days are shown by week. Spending: choosing a category now asks each time whether to remember the merchant; category menus load only when a row is edited, and the list shows 300 rows at a time. Renamed accounts show their new name in selectors. Layout: tables are as wide as their contents and centered in the card, headers are left aligned, numbers/$/% are right aligned and other cells left aligned, and page side margins are 25% wider. Settings: Info sits just above Close.

Fix: updating the packaged program no longer leaves a white, “Not Responding” window: the old copy now starts the new one fully detached and then ends itself, and the restart is written to tracker.log. Accounts: a chequing, savings, credit card or line-of-credit account can be changed to any of those types from its edit bar (its entries, remembered type and opening balance follow). An account with no transactions is removed automatically when another account has the same account ID (the empty twin left behind after reloading). Spending: the Uncategorized card counts every uncategorized transaction whatever the date range, and clicking it lists them all.

Start-up checks: the start-up window now appears only when a check fails, and a new check looks on GitHub for a newer version; when there is one, a bar under the top menu says so (Update / Dismiss) and a dot appears by the version number. Being offline is not a failure. Line of credit: the balance starts at $0, taking money out makes it negative and counts as owed, payments bring it back to $0, and an overpayment is a positive balance that does not reduce other liabilities (credit cards are unchanged); “Real balance today” and “Opening balance” replace the owed wording (owing $10,000 is -10000) and existing lines are converted. Transactions lists (Spending and Transactions): a tick box on every line and a select-all box; the Edit, Split and Delete buttons are gone from the lines. Ticking one line shows its Edit / Split / Delete bar under it; ticking several shows a bar at the bottom with the count, Change category (Spending entries; the merchants are remembered) and Delete, and Shift-click selects a range. Accounts page: Investment accounts and Chequing and savings accounts are separate tables with only the columns that apply (Name, Type, Ownership, value or interest rate, cash, % of net worth); every table is read-only until you click a row, which opens an edit bar with the other fields (account ID, real cash today, closed, ignore in net worth, transaction count, Delete); chequing and savings accounts have an Ownership setting and can be deleted together with their imported entries, as can credit cards and lines of credit; chequing and savings are no longer listed under Assets here (they still count in the Overview’s asset total). Assets and Liabilities work the same way. Margin page: Margin interest takes a third of the width next to the monthly card, same height, hiding Statement dates and then stacking on narrow windows. Spending chart: clicking a daily point opens that day; the card titles above the charts are removed; Transactions remembers whether you last viewed Spending or Investing. Retirement: the year-by-year table no longer has scroll bars.

Update from GitHub: the Update page shows the installed version and the newest published version, lists every version in the public releases repository (DarrenS01/InvestTrackerApp_public) and lets you choose any of them, including an older one. You confirm first; your data is backed up, the file is downloaded and checked against its SHA-256, then installed and the program restarts. The packaged program takes the ready-made InvestTracker.exe when one is published (no Python needed) and otherwise builds from the source zip as before. A GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) builds the Windows exe and publishes it with the source zip and index.json whenever tracker/version.py changes on main (needs the PUBLIC_REPO_TOKEN secret). Choosing a file on the Update page still works.
